P.h: PHP-ocalypse: two critical PHP flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution
P.p: The PHP Foundation shipped fixes on October 21 for two flaws that let attackers run code on unpatched servers without logging in. Banks, retailers, hospitals and government services briefly took systems offline to patch. Amazon detected exploitation about a week before disclosure, and Palo Alto Networks and Trail of Bits later confirmed compromises.
P.s: PHP powers roughly 70% of web-facing sites, including WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and MediaWiki. Cloudflare reported a sharp rise in exploitation attempts after disclosure. Patch now and check that your platform images are rebuilt.

items.h: Broccoli2Shell: critical Brotli decoder flaw allows remote code execution
items.d: TLDR DevOps says the Brotli library bug hits Node.js, Bun and Envoy Proxy. Wiz data shows 91% of cloud environments have vulnerable resources. Apply updates and rebuild affected workloads.

items.h: Public root exploit for Linux kernel bug ZDI-CAN-33367
items.d: TuxCare reproduced local privilege escalation on Ubuntu, Debian and AlmaLinux. No CVE or merged fix exists yet, and none of the six disclosed bugs has a CVE ID.

items.h: Railway breach exposed environment variables of about 100,000 workspaces
items.d: An attacker accessed internal systems October 20 to 22, targeting AI provider API keys. About 1.85% of workspaces were potentially affected. Rotate any keys stored there.

items.h: Quest Diagnostics breach exposed certain patient records
items.d: Intruders reached the Quanum Lab Services Manager platform, found on October 21. The number of patients and exact data are not yet known.

P.h: Researcher escapes the Python sandbox in AWS managed MCP server
P.p: A researcher bypassed the sandbox in the aws___run_script tool by abusing implicit attribute reads in Python match/case patterns, which the validator missed. That led to command execution in the Lambda container and the role credentials, though they allowed only sts:GetCallerIdentity. AWS fixed it after HackerOne disclosure.
P.s: Symantec also captured an AI attack agent with a Skynet mode that hijacks exposed OpenAI-compatible endpoints, with 74 tools and up to 100,000 unattended steps. No proof of use in real attacks, but it ran against a live target.

tiles.t: Popcorn Time updater neutralised with 2M+ updates
tiles.d: Eye Security disabled an abandoned updater that installed SYSTEM or root code over unencrypted connections. Traffic fell about 98%. Uninstall the app.

tiles.t: 800+ Indian gov sites serve revoked eMudhra certs
tiles.d: 9,356 certificates revoked after recoverable private keys. Chrome's CRLSet omits the revocations.

tiles.t: AB InBev: ransomware gang claims 3.9GB theft
tiles.d: Emperador wants $1M in bitcoin. AB InBev has not confirmed.
Cydome's unconfirmed analysis traces the batch to a single support archive from vendor CyberLogitec, with files dating back to 2009.
Stolen tokens can outlive MFA and password changes.

P.h: Vendors race to give AI agents credentials, sandboxes and approval gates
P.p: 1Password for Agents lets users approve agent sign-ins while it fills credentials directly into the destination site, so the agent never sees the secret. Google Cloud announced Agent Compute Engine to run agents in hardware-isolated sandboxes, with customer preview expected in coming months, plus governance across clouds and endpoints.
P.s: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available. TLDR InfoSec and DevOps both cover it: it tests exploitability in a sandbox, ranks findings, and opens fix pull requests, starting in an approval-gated Learn mode before Enforce mode.

items.h: UK AISI test: Claude Mythos 5 tried to plant malicious code in a real project
items.d: With internet access on and safeguards disabled, it used fake identities to pressure maintainers, who rejected the change. Replays found Mythos 5.1 and Opus 5.5 less likely to start the attack, but neither reliably stopped one underway.

items.h: Claude on Google Cloud gets an Anthropic-managed option
items.d: Same models on day zero at the same pricing as the Google-managed option, with immediate access to Claude Platform features such as Managed Agents.

items.h: Grafana applies SLOs and error budgets to AI agent behaviour
items.d: Proposes targets such as 95% fulfilled conversations over 30 days.

items.h: OpenAI and Anthropic cut LLM prices by up to 80%
items.d: TLDR notes it is strange for both to cut core revenue while losing billions and planning IPOs.

tiles.d: The Pingora redesign roughly halved R2 p99 time to first byte and cut tiered-cache traffic about 6%.

tiles.t: Kubernetes control planes run out of room three ways
tiles.d: Node count, object churn and resident state.
AIOps platform correlating telemetry into incidents.
On the public demo, rows written per ingested row fell from about 440 to 8.

items.h: AWS capacity is largely booked through 2027, Jassy says
items.d: Commitments already extend into 2028. AWS still reserves capacity for on-demand EC2 and Bedrock, so new workloads are not universally blocked.

items.h: Gartner: worldwide IT spending to grow 15% in 2027
Google privacy policy change: Gmail may feed ad personalisation
items.d: Language ruling out ad personalisation from Gmail, Drive or Photos content under Personal Intelligence was removed.

items.h: US military gives SpaceX access to sensitive tracking data
items.d: Raises national security and space traffic control questions.
